KEY MESSAGE 1... The dog days of summer are upon us with several
days of hot temps and humid conditions forecast for ENC. The key
will be how widespread these conditions will be over the next
few days. Latest surface analysis shows surface high noted 
across the Southeast with the previously mentioned stalled 
frontal boundary currently along the Hwy 64 corridor this 
morning with shower and thunderstorm activity riding from NW to 
SE along the northern periphery of this boundary across portions
of eastern VA into our offshore waters. Much of this activity 
has remained rather weak and expect this to continue over the 
next several hours with much of the activity remaining offshore.
Temps this morning remain around the 70s to near 80 with light 
and variable winds.

Aforementioned front will eventually sag southward across the 
region today, although how far south and how quick remains 
uncertain. The NAM being the slowest and furthest north solution
barely getting the front south of the Hwy 70 corridor by this
evening. While the HRRR and CMC push the front further south 
slightly faster getting south of the Crystal Coast by this 
afternoon. This will offer some relative relief over the 
weekend, but locations along and south of Highway 70 have the 
highest probability of seeing HI values at or exceeding 105F 
both today and Sunday. Will note coolest temps will likely be 
found along the NOBX where highs in the mid 80s are forecast 
today under steady NE flow. The frontal boundary will then lift 
back across the Mid-Atlantic on Sun/Mon as a warm front, 
entrenching the entire FA again in potentially dangerous heat 
and humidity as highs climb back into the upper 90s. While we 
look to have a cold front track across the region Mon night into
Tue it wont cool the area much with temps remaining in the 90s 
into the end of next week and with dewpoints remaining in the 
mid to upper 70s as well, HI of 105F+ will be common across ENC
to varying degrees each day. 

Heat Advisories remain in effect starting at 11AM today and
continuing into 8PM this evening. Depending on convective 
coverage this afternoon we may see an early cancellation of this
heat advisory but that would be dependent on how much
thunderstorm activity we get this afternoon. We continue to 
encourage anyone planning on spending time outdoors to stay 
hydrated and to limit exposure to the heat, if able.

KEY MESSAGE 2...As mentioned above, frontal boundary is 
currently noted along our far northern zones with shower and 
tstm activity riding along the northern periphery of this front.
Forecast calls for this front to drop south today with some 
uncertainty with how fast and how far south this front gets 
before stalling over or just south of ENC. Much like yesterday, 
several boxes are checked to support at least scattered shower 
and thunderstorm activity with MLCAPES around 1500-2500 J/kg, 
PWAT's above 2", and a slight increase in deep layer shear 
especially around the front (closer to 25-30 kts). The one main
difference compared to yesterday is we have the front around 
the area today, which should help to provide a focal point for 
thunderstorm activity across the region this afternoon and 
evening. Current forecast suggests a mainly dry morning with 
shower and thunderstorm chances increasing as the afternoon 
wears on as daily sea/river/sound breezes interact with the 
incoming front. Ended up keeping SChc to high end Chc PoPs in 
the forecast today given uncertainty with frontal placement and 
much like yesterday poor CAM agreement in coverage of 
thunderstorms today. WRF NSSL and FV3 being the most aggressive
while the NAM3K/HRRR being slightly drier. Any activity that 
does develop should gradually weaken and dissipate as the 
evening wears on. Then as we get into Sunday another round of 
shower and thunderstorm activity will be possible as this 
stalled front then lifts north as a warm front but once again
uncertainty with precip coverage remains high. So the activity 
will certainly be very hit or miss today and tomorrow. 

For both today and tomorrow the convective evolution will be 
heavily driven by mesoscale factors owing to the low confidence
precip forecast and therefore thunderstorm forecast each day. 
Strongest storms could bring a damaging wind threat, frequent 
lightning, and torrential rainfall. The bottom line is the 
overall environment will remain at least marginally favorable 
for stronger storms and a flooding risk through the weekend, 
wherever activity manages to develop.

KEY MESSAGE 3... A second front is then forecast to track across
the area on Mon into Tue with this front currently having a
higher chance at sweeping across all of ENC and bringing a 
favorable environment for additional rounds of scattered shower
and thunderstorm activity with a few of these storms 
potentially becoming strong to severe in nature. Still several
